name: Derek Sivers’ "Hell Yeah or No" Filter
diagnostic: Over-commitment paralysis and middle-tier opportunity dilution. Agreeing to marginally interesting obligations that eat up the space needed for exceptional opportunities.

procedure.text: For any new invitation or optional initiative, rate your enthusiasm from 1 to 10.
Anything below an unconditional 9 or 10 gets a polite, decisive no.
Drop the social guilt: every middle-tier yes rejects a future breakthrough.
Keep a short rejection template so drafting does not slow you down.

trap: Applying the filter to obligations that need discipline rather than enthusiasm, such as taxes or security patches.
procedureFull:
1. When assessing any new inbound invite, collaboration opportunity, or non-critical initiative, evaluate personal intuitive enthusiasm on a 1-to-10 scale.
2. If the internal response is anything lower than an unconditional "9" or "10" ("Hell Yeah!"), default immediately to a polite, decisive "No."
3. Strip away social guilt: realize that every middle-tier acceptance is an implicit rejection of future breakthroughs.
4. Maintain an explicit template for neutral, rapid rejections to eliminate drafting hesitation.
setupFull: "Thank you for the thoughtful invitation. Given my active focus on completing our core distributed engine deliverable, I am unavailable to take on auxiliary projects or speaking commitments for the foreseeable future. Best of success with the initiative."
trapFull: Applying the filter to foundational operational responsibilities (e.g., filing taxes, patching critical security bugs) that require disciplined execution rather than emotional enthusiasm.
